verdicts.quote: Add `waiting_on_requester` as an active status. Allow `in_progress → waiting_on_requester`, and from waiting allow `in_progress` or `resolved`.
at or after 72 elapsed hours in `waiting_on_requester` … The policy uses status entry rather than any subsequent ticket edit. … regardless of a title or priority edit during the wait.
One reminder per continuous waiting period is the default policy. … Resume before the first deadline and observe no reminder for that period. Re-enter waiting and the clock starts again.

from waiting allow `in_progress` or `resolved`. … regardless of a title or priority edit during the wait. … Leaving waiting cancels an outstanding reminder … Reply ingestion and remote relay operation are outside the implementation scope.
send a reminder through the existing outbox and notifier to the requester's stored address. … The message includes ticket ID and title and asks the requester to reply with needed information.
verdicts.missing: The subject and body format, whether to show elapsed waiting time, and what address to use when the requester field is free text are unspecified.

verdicts.quote: Preserve all existing transitions and ordinary resolution notification. … The message includes ticket ID and title and asks the requester to reply with needed information.
the single existing worker loop per CONTRIBUTING. When enabled and healthy, the first tick at or after expiry queues and attempts delivery.

preserves wait entry and the prior reminder's identity. … Sent, exhausted or cancelled reminders do not generate a new event for the same wait. … key/ID deduplication covers the existing crash window between delivery and attempt recording.

A nonwaiting ticket never qualifies. … Leaving waiting cancels an outstanding reminder so that the worker cannot send it later, even after re-entry. … the first tick at or after expiry queues and attempts delivery.
A failed delivery uses existing backoff and retry limits. Sent, exhausted or cancelled reminders do not generate a new event for the same wait.
verdicts.missing: Whether a reminder template must exist before the worker can enqueue the event is unspecified.

verdicts.quote: One reminder per continuous waiting period … Re-enter waiting and the clock starts again. Two eligible periods have distinct reminder keys, even when entry times are equal. Resolving before delivery also ends the waiting period.
At the first enabled worker tick at or after 72 elapsed hours in `waiting_on_requester` … Check with the injected clock, temporary data file and local transport.
verdicts.missing: The clock source used in production to record entry and compare elapsed time is unspecified.

verdicts.quote: With DATA_FILE enabled, reopening the service preserves wait entry and the prior reminder's identity.

verdicts.quote: Version 1 data files created before this feature remain readable.

verdicts.quote: Existing caller access governs API reads and mutations.
